text.p: Following are the highlights of the main stories in the Bosnian press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Federation finance minister Drago Bilandzija says about $374 million in aid funds were not disbursed through implementing agencies and there is no information about where the money went.
- Bosnia's central bank will start to operate on August 11, when the new currency, the convertible mark, is due to become a legal currency, officials said.
- The Moslem-Croat federation government ordered a duty free shop at the Izacici border crossing near Bihac to close down due to a lack of proper legal documents.
- Some 5,000 miners employed in central Bosnia went on strike on Wednesday night, protesting over a delay in salary payments.

- The board of directors for Sarajevo's tobacco factory sent a letter to the federation prime minister protesting over the trade minister's decision to treat cigarettes produced in Croatia as domestic products.
- There are about 336,000 people who are unemployed in the Moslem-Croat federation, the director of Bosnia's statistics bureau, Hasan Zolic, said.
- Hungary and Slovenia, unlike other European countries and the United States, said they will not suspend contacts with Bosnia's embassies. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
